title: Error semantics for agents
description: Emitted on stderr when JSON errors mode is active (--json, global --output-format json, or effective JSON on scp/tunnel). Not a success payload. Agents MUST use retryable/error_class before re-invoking (Rules Rust retry/backoff).

exit_code.description: Process exit code following sysexits-inspired mapping

message.description: Error text carried inside the JSON envelope on stderr. Always English, regardless of --lang or the host locale: this is a stable contract, not a localized string. Branch on error_code, never on this prose. Localization applies only to human text mode (--output-format text), where the label is translated and this same detail is preserved verbatim.

remote_exit_code.description: Optional remote shell exit when process exit is EX_GENERAL (1) after non-zero remote command

error_code.description: Stable machine-oriented discriminator (`partial_failure`, `unavailable`, `software`, `io`, `authentication_failed`, …). Branch on this, never on `message`. Present on every failure envelope; it was emitted long before it was contracted here.

error_class.description: High-level class: transient (agent may re-invoke with backoff), permanent (fix inputs), cancelled (signal/pipe), partial (multi-host fan-out where some targets succeeded — re-running the whole batch repeats the work that already landed, so inspect per-host detail instead). `partial` shipped with G-ERR-R02 and was missing from this enum, which meant a strict validator rejected the very envelope the CLI emits.

retryable.description: True only when the same argv may succeed after backoff (exit 74 transport/timeout). Never true for auth (77), usage (64), or remote command (1)

suggestion.description: Optional short remediation hint for agents

target_resolved.description: Canonical name for the host this process had resolved when the failure occurred (Explicit Target Designation). Bind new consumers to this field; `host_resolved` is the 0.5.5 spelling, emitted from the same value as a read alias. Present on the single-host exec family and on every scp/sftp transfer, including sftp filesystem verbs. Absent — not empty — when the failure happened before a target was chosen.

target_source.description: Canonical name for how target_resolved was obtained. `argv` means the caller typed it in this invocation; `active_marker` means it was inherited from the file `connect` wrote, under the explicit --use-active opt-in; `selector` means it came from --all/--hosts/--tags. Transfers never reach the marker, so they report `argv` or `selector` only.

host_resolved.description: Compatibility alias of target_resolved (0.5.5 spelling), written from the same value and never an independent source of truth. Host this process had resolved when the failure occurred (GAP-SSH-EXEC-ENVELOPE-002). Absent — not empty — when the failure happened before a target was chosen, which is the case for most usage errors and for vps_not_found. An empty string would assert that a host was chosen and has no name; absence says no host was chosen at all. Present on the single-host exec family; the fleet path names every host in its batch entries instead.

host_source.description: Compatibility alias of target_source (0.5.5 spelling). How host_resolved was obtained. `argv` means the caller typed it in this invocation; `active_marker` means it was inherited from the file `connect` wrote, under the explicit --use-active opt-in; `selector` means it came from --all/--hosts/--tags. Comparing this between two runs is what turns a misdirected execution from an investigation into a string comparison.

active_fallback.description: True when target_resolved came from the active marker rather than argv, under the explicit --use-active opt-in. Redundant with target_source on purpose: a shell pipeline can branch on a boolean without knowing how the enum is spelled. The 0.5.5 aliases host_resolved and host_source carry the same values.
